standard.title: Text connectives and cohesion
standard.description: identify how text connectives including temporal and conditional words, and topic word associations are used to sequence and connect ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how paragraphs group related information within stages of written texts (AC9E3LA04). They have not yet identified text connectives as the explicit devices that sequence and connect ideas across sentences and sections.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify temporal, conditional and additive text connectives, explain their role in sequencing and connecting ideas, and recognise how pronouns and determiners maintain cohesion across a text.

nodes.label: Pronouns and determiners as cohesive links
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how pronouns and determiners link back to previously mentioned information in a text.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify a pronoun or determiner (this, that, these, those) in a text and explain what it refers back to.
nodes.typical_width: Identify multiple cohesive devices — pronouns and demonstrative determiners — across a text and explain how they keep the reader connected to the subject without repetition.
wider: Examine how cohesion breaks down in texts where pronoun reference is unclear, and revise to restore it
Compare how pronouns and determiners create cohesion differently in narrative versus informational texts

response_modes.reason: Students often read past pronouns without tracking their referents. Identifying the reference chain requires sustained attention and practice — this is a fluency-building node, not a conceptual one.

success_criteria: Can identify a pronoun in a text and name the noun it refers back to
Can identify a demonstrative determiner (this/that/these/those) and explain what it is pointing to

nodes.label: Connectives between sentences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify text connectives that create logical links between sentences and explain the relationship each signals.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify a sentence-level connective (e.g. however, therefore, in addition) and explain the relationship it signals between the two sentences.
nodes.typical_width: Identify a range of connective types — adversative (however, nevertheless), causal (therefore, as a result), additive (in addition, furthermore) — across informational texts and explain what logical relationship each signals.
wider: Compare how connectives are used in argument texts versus explanation texts — which types predominate and why
Examine how removing or substituting connectives changes the logic of a paragraph, using a range of text types

response_modes.reason: Students often know 'however means contrast' but apply it mechanically without understanding the claim-counter relationship it creates. Multiple text contexts showing connectives doing real logical work helps build genuine functional understanding.

success_criteria: Can identify a connective and name the type of relationship it signals (contrast, cause, addition)
Does not treat all connectives as interchangeable — can explain why substituting 'however' for 'therefore' changes meaning

nodes.label: Temporal connectives and sequencing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify temporal connectives and explain how they sequence events or steps through time.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify temporal connectives (firstly, then, next, finally) in a text and explain how they signal sequence.
nodes.typical_width: Identify temporal connectives across sequential texts — procedures, recounts, explanations — and explain how they create a clear time-ordered structure that guides the reader.
wider: Compare temporal sequencing in a recount (past sequence) versus a procedure (imperative sequence) and explain how the text type changes the connective choices
Examine how First Nations Australian oral narrative traditions use temporal sequencing in storytelling, and compare with written sequential texts
success_criteria: Can identify at least three temporal connectives in a sequence text and explain the order they create
Understands that temporal connectives signal time relationships, not just list items
